newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Piltel falls by 10.2 pct to new low.
newsitem.headline: Piltel falls by 10.2 pct to new low.

text.p: Cellular phone company Pilipino Telephone Co (Piltel) plunged to a new record low of 8.80 pesos, down one peso, or 10.2 percent, in early trade on Friday.
Analysts said Piltel was pulled down by its poor first quarter earnings that prompted brokerage firms to downgrade their full-year forecasts.
"People were hoping it could still rise. But since the market dropped, those who are holding out are selling now at whatever price," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
Piltel was the most heavily traded issue in mid-session.
Piltel reported last month that its net income in the first three months of 1997 was at 42.6 million pesos from 246.6 million in the same period last year.
All Asia Securities research director Helen Alvarez said she downgraded Piltel's net income projection for 1997 to 750 milion pesos from an original 947 million.
Piltel is one of five cellular phone companies in the Philippines. It was the first to admit to problems of cloning.
"Piltel is also a classic example of a stock beleaguered by the general weakness of the market," Alvarez said.
